title: Herod and His Family
lead: Herod the Great, king of Judea under Rome from 37 to 4 BC, and the sons and grandsons who ruled parts of his kingdom after him. Several men in the New Testament called "Herod" are different members of this family.

sections.b: Herod the Great (king 37–4 BC) rebuilt the Temple and ruled when Jesus was born (Matthew 2:1; Luke 1:5). At his death Rome divided his kingdom among three sons: Archelaus, ethnarch of Judea, Samaria and Idumea (4 BC–AD 6, Matthew 2:22), removed by Augustus; Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee and Perea (4 BC–AD 39), who executed John the Baptist (Matthew 14:1–12) and met Jesus at his trial (Luke 23:7–12); and Philip, tetrarch of the lands northeast of the Sea of Galilee (Luke 3:1). Herod Agrippa I, a grandson, killed James son of Zebedee (Acts 12:1–23); his son Agrippa II heard Paul (Acts 25–26).
